changes.quote: > 60-month term must have a minimum book value of $7,500 unless: Vehicle is 2-3 years old with 60,000-80,000 miles; must have minimum book value of $12,000
changes.note: The minimum-book-value gates on terms over 60 months were missing entirely. A 2-3 year old unit with 60-80K miles, or a 3-7 year old with 80-100K, needs $12,000 of book to go past 60 months — otherwise the floor is $7,500. The record had the term table but not the book-value condition on it. Also adds the dealer advance formula and the 30-day unfunded return, which sends the contract back.

changes.quote: A nonrefundable acquisition fee may be assessed for each contract based on the customer's credit risk. Acquisition fees cannot be charged to the customer.
changes.note: The record had the $150 assignment fee. The sheet also describes a separate risk-based acquisition fee — two different charges, neither passable to the customer. Also that subvented contracts follow the manufacturer program rather than these guidelines.

ambiguities.note: The 10-row x 3-mileage-band maximum term table is complete and matches the sheet. So do the GAP rules the document itself flags as updated in this revision (no purchase under 70% advance, 80% in Indiana, $1,500 or state max, no NY indirect, no GAP or CL&D for covered service members in California) — the record is current on the one thing this revision changed. The $150 assignment fee, the 70/30 split, the $200 buy-rate flat, the 3-payment/3-cycle chargeback and the Canadian A/B tier LTVs are all right. And p11's state map is in the record correctly, as established on 2026-08-26.

Record says "Current/future year, <=7,500 miles (non-GM <=5,000 mi)". Page 2 speaks only of a value adjustment above 5,000 miles (6,500 for Triton) and does not define new vs used by mileage. The 7,500 figure may come from a page I did not read closely or another document. Left alone and added the value-adjustment rule as its own row rather than overwriting.
